title: MITCHELL-RILEY SYNDROME
alt_titles: DIABETES, NEONATAL, WITH PANCREATIC HYPOPLASIA, INTESTINAL ATRESIA, AND GALLBLADDER APLASIA OR HYPOPLASIA

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Mitchell-Riley syndrome (MTCHRS) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the RFX6 gene (612659) on chromosome 6q22.1.

checks.claim: Mitchell-Riley syndrome (MTCHRS) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the RFX6 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We propose to name their condition, now of defined molecular aetiology, the Mitchell-Riley syndrome after the two clinicians who first described it.
checks.explanation: The paper reports homozygous RFX6 mutations in probands 1, 2, 4 and 5, and a compound heterozygous mutation in proband 3. It names the condition Mitchell-Riley syndrome.

checks.claim: The RFX6 gene is located on chromosome 6q22.1.
checks.evidence_quote: Of these genes, only RFX6, which falls in the largest segment at 6q21-22, had pancreas–enriched expression in the TiGER database
checks.explanation: The paper places RFX6 at 6q21-22. The draft's 6q22.1 is the standard band designation, so it counts as a restatement.

paragraphs.text: Mitchell-Riley syndrome is a disorder that presents in the neonatal period and was suggested to be autosomal recessive by Mitchell et al. (2004). Its main features are neonatal diabetes mellitus with a hypoplastic or annular pancreas, intestinal atresia (duodenal, jejunal, or both), and aplasia or hypoplasia of the gallbladder (Mitchell et al., 2004). Some patients have intestinal malrotation (Galán-Gómez et al., 2007), biliary abnormalities (Martínez-Frías et al., 1992), and chronic diarrhea or malabsorption (Smith et al., 2010).

checks.claim: Mitchell-Riley syndrome presents in the neonatal period.
checks.evidence_quote: Five infants (two sibling pairs from two families, and an isolated case) presented with neonatal diabetes, hypoplastic or annular pancreas, jejunal atresia, duodenal atresia and gall bladder aplasia or hypoaplasia.
checks.explanation: The infants presented with neonatal diabetes, so the condition presents in the neonatal period.

checks.claim: Mitchell et al. (2004) suggested that Mitchell-Riley syndrome is autosomal recessive.
checks.evidence_quote: probably represents a new autosomal recessive syndrome involving a genetic abnormality that interferes with normal islet development
checks.explanation: The authors propose autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: A main feature of Mitchell-Riley syndrome is neonatal diabetes mellitus with a hypoplastic or annular pancreas.
checks.evidence_quote: presented with neonatal diabetes, hypoplastic or annular pancreas, jejunal atresia, duodenal atresia and gall bladder aplasia or hypoaplasia
checks.explanation: Neonatal diabetes with a hypoplastic or annular pancreas is listed among the features.

checks.claim: A main feature of Mitchell-Riley syndrome is intestinal atresia that is duodenal, jejunal, or both.
checks.evidence_quote: presented with neonatal diabetes, hypoplastic or annular pancreas, jejunal atresia, duodenal atresia and gall bladder aplasia or hypoaplasia
checks.explanation: Both jejunal and duodenal atresia are listed. The abstract doesn't say which infant had which.

checks.claim: A main feature of Mitchell-Riley syndrome is aplasia or hypoplasia of the gallbladder.
checks.evidence_quote: jejunal atresia, duodenal atresia and gall bladder aplasia or hypoaplasia
checks.explanation: Gallbladder aplasia or hypoplasia is listed among the features.

checks.claim: Some patients with Mitchell-Riley syndrome have intestinal malrotation.
checks.evidence_quote: presented with an MCA pattern characterized by low birth weight, duodenal atresia, extrahepatic biliary atresia, hypoplastic pancreas and intestinal malrotation
checks.explanation: The abstract describes one patient with intestinal malrotation together with duodenal atresia, biliary atresia and a hypoplastic pancreas. The paper calls the disorder Martínez-Frías syndrome, which OMIM treats as the same condition as Mitchell-Riley syndrome, so this backs the statement that some patients have malrotation.

checks.claim: Some patients with Mitchell-Riley syndrome have biliary abnormalities.
checks.evidence_quote: We studied 2 sibs, born to consanguineous parents, who presented with an MCA pattern which includes low birthweight, tracheoesophageal fistula, duodenal atresia, extrahepatic biliary atresia, hypoplastic pancreas, and hypospadias.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports extrahepatic biliary atresia, a biliary abnormality, in 2 sibs who also had duodenal atresia and a hypoplastic pancreas. The paper is from 1992 and does not use the name Mitchell-Riley syndrome. It describes the condition as a previously unreported autosomal recessive syndrome and does not mention neonatal diabetes. Treating these sibs as Mitchell-Riley patients is the draft's reading, not something this abstract says.

checks.claim: Some patients with Mitchell-Riley syndrome have chronic diarrhea or malabsorption.
checks.evidence_quote: In addition, the syndrome involves hypoplastic gall bladder, and intractable diarrhea unresponsive to pancreatic enzyme replacement.
checks.explanation: The Discussion also mentions 'severe intestinal malabsorption'.

paragraphs.text: Mitchell et al. (2004) described 5 infants with a new syndrome of neonatal diabetes, a hypoplastic or annular pancreas, duodenal or jejunal atresia, and aplasia or hypoplasia of the gallbladder. One sib pair was born to consanguineous parents. Mitchell et al. (2004) concluded that the condition probably represented a new autosomal recessive syndrome. Four of the infants died in the first year of life.

checks.claim: Mitchell et al. (2004) described 5 infants with a new syndrome of neonatal diabetes, hypoplastic or annular pancreas, duodenal or jejunal atresia, and aplasia or hypoplasia of the gallbladder.
checks.evidence_quote: Five infants (two sibling pairs from two families, and an isolated case) presented with neonatal diabetes, hypoplastic or annular pancreas, jejunal atresia, duodenal atresia and gall bladder aplasia or hypoaplasia.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes five infants with these features.

checks.claim: Among the 5 infants described by Mitchell et al. (2004), one sib pair was born to consanguineous parents.
checks.evidence_quote: One sibling pair was born to consanguineous parents.
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: Mitchell et al. (2004) concluded that the syndrome of neonatal diabetes, pancreatic hypoplasia, intestinal atresia, and gallbladder aplasia probably represented a new autosomal recessive syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: This combination of multiple congenital abnormalities has not been previously described and probably represents a new autosomal recessive syndrome
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract's conclusions.

checks.claim: Four of the 5 infants described by Mitchell et al. (2004) died in the first year of life.
checks.evidence_quote: Four children died in the first year of life despite aggressive medical management.
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: Mitchell et al. (2004) suggested that Mitchell-Riley syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder; in their report, one affected sib pair was born to consanguineous parents. Smith et al. (2010) confirmed autosomal recessive inheritance by finding biallelic RFX6 mutations in affected individuals, each inherited from carrier parents.

checks.claim: Mitchell et al. (2004) suggested that Mitchell-Riley syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: probably represents a new autosomal recessive syndrome involving a genetic abnormality that interferes with normal islet development
checks.explanation: The authors propose autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: In the report of Mitchell et al. (2004), one sib pair affected with Mitchell-Riley syndrome was born to consanguineous parents.
checks.evidence_quote: One sibling pair was born to consanguineous parents.
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2010) confirmed autosomal recessive inheritance of Mitchell-Riley syndrome by finding biallelic RFX6 mutations in affected individuals.
checks.evidence_quote: In human infants with a similar autosomal recessive syndrome of neonatal diabetes, genetic mapping and subsequent sequencing identified mutations in the human RFX6 gene.
checks.explanation: Every proband with a mutation had two mutant alleles: either homozygous or compound heterozygous.

checks.claim: In the Mitchell-Riley syndrome patients studied by Smith et al. (2010), each RFX6 mutation was inherited from a carrier parent.
checks.evidence_quote: All mutations were inherited from carrier parents.
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Smith et al. (2010) found homozygous or compound heterozygous mutations in the RFX6 gene in patients with Mitchell-Riley syndrome, and linked some of their probands to previous clinical case reports. They identified the gene by homozygosity mapping in consanguineous families followed by candidate gene sequencing. RFX6 encodes a winged-helix transcription factor. Smith et al. (2010) showed that RFX6 is expressed in the developing gut endoderm and in the pancreatic endocrine lineage, and that it acts downstream of NGN3 in islet cell development.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2010) found homozygous or compound heterozygous mutations in the RFX6 gene in patients with Mitchell-Riley syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Proband #3, still alive at the age of 9 and intermittently off insulin, was a compound heterozygote for donor-site loss in intron 6 (IVS6+2 t>g) and disruption of the acceptor site in intron 1 (IVS1-12 a>g).
checks.explanation: Probands 1, 2, 4 and 5 were homozygous and proband 3 was compound heterozygous.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2010) linked some of their Mitchell-Riley syndrome probands with RFX6 mutations to previous clinical case reports.
checks.evidence_quote: (see Supplementary material for pedigree information and references to previous clinical case reports)
checks.explanation: The paper links its probands to previously published clinical case reports.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2010) identified RFX6 as the Mitchell-Riley syndrome gene by homozygosity mapping in consanguineous families followed by candidate gene sequencing.
checks.evidence_quote: The disease locus was mapped using overlapping homozygosity in probands #1and #2 (see Supplementary material for pedigree information and references to previous clinical case reports) respectively the offspring of first and second cousins.
checks.explanation: The homozygosity mapping is supported. After mapping, the paper used both unbiased deep sequencing of all exons in the shared homozygous regions and direct sequencing of RFX6, not only candidate gene sequencing.

checks.claim: RFX6 encodes a winged-helix transcription factor.
checks.evidence_quote: we identified Rfx6, a member of the RFX (Regulatory Factor X-box binding) family of winged-helix transcription factors.
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2010) showed that RFX6 is expressed in the developing gut endoderm.
checks.evidence_quote: Rfx6 is expressed initially broadly in the definitive endoderm after gastrulation, becomes restricted to the gut and pancreatic bud at mid gestation
checks.explanation: The paper shows expression in the developing gut endoderm.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2010) showed that RFX6 is expressed in the pancreatic endocrine lineage.
checks.evidence_quote: demonstrating restricted expression of Rfx6 in the endocrine lineage even at this early stage
checks.explanation: The paper shows expression in the pancreatic endocrine lineage.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2010) showed that RFX6 acts downstream of NGN3 in islet cell development.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we show that the transcription factor Rfx6 directs islet cell differentiation downstream of Neurog3.
checks.explanation: The paper places Rfx6 downstream of Neurogenin3 (NGN3).

paragraphs.text: Sansbury et al. (2015) reported patients with biallelic RFX6 mutations and a milder phenotype, in whom the diagnosis of diabetes was not made in the neonatal period.

checks.claim: Sansbury et al. (2015) reported patients with biallelic RFX6 mutations and a milder phenotype than classic Mitchell-Riley syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Aside from the difference in age of onset of diabetes in the two new cases, the phenotype differed from previously published cases in the absence of any liver pathology, although one of the cases (case 1) had absent gall bladder. This relatively milder phenotype
checks.explanation: The paper describes the biallelic (compound heterozygous) cases as having a relatively milder phenotype than previously reported Mitchell-Riley syndrome cases.

checks.claim: In the patients with biallelic RFX6 mutations reported by Sansbury et al. (2015), diabetes was not diagnosed in the neonatal period.
checks.evidence_quote: These new cases are the first with Mitchell–Riley syndrome in whom the diagnosis of diabetes was not made in the neonatal period, all other cases to date having been diagnosed within the first 2 weeks of life.
checks.explanation: Diabetes was diagnosed at ages 3 and 6 years.

paragraphs.text: Smith et al. (2010) found that Rfx6-null mice died shortly after birth. The mice failed to generate any of the normal islet cell types, including insulin-producing beta cells, except for pancreatic polypeptide-producing cells.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2010) found that Rfx6-null mice died shortly after birth.
checks.evidence_quote: homozygous Rfx6eGFPcre/eGFPcre mice were born at the expected Mendelian ratio, but failed to feed normally, exhibited gross bowel distension due to small bowel obstruction (Fig. 3e-f) and died within 2 days post partum.
checks.explanation: Death within 2 days of birth matches 'shortly after birth'.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2010) found that Rfx6-null mice failed to generate any of the normal islet cell types, including insulin-producing beta cells, except pancreatic polypeptide-producing cells.
checks.evidence_quote: Mice lacking Rfx6 failed to generate any of the normal islet cell types except for pancreatic-polypeptide-producing cells.
checks.explanation: The full text also confirms that no cells expressed insulin, glucagon, somatostatin or ghrelin.
